# Spending per pupil

## Cambridge and Salem — the group's two smallest districts — have held the top two spots every year

In 2024–25 Cambridge spent about **$31,000 per K-12 pupil** in current
operating funds, against a five-district average near $30,000. Cambridge and
Salem, the group's two smallest districts, have traded first and second place
in all ten years shown — small districts spread fixed costs (a principal, a
building, a bus route) over fewer students, so their higher spending per pupil
is arithmetic, not inefficiency. Dollars are adjusted for inflation and shown
in 2024–25 dollars. They exclude capital projects, debt service, and interfund
transfers; see [Methods](../appendix/methods.qmd) for the definitions.

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.getcwd())

import polars as pl
from plotnine import (
    aes,
    geom_line,
    geom_point,
    ggplot,
    labs,
    scale_color_manual,
    scale_x_continuous,
    scale_y_continuous,
)
from great_tables import GT, loc, md, style

import comparisons as cc

# Format axis/break values as whole dollars.
def _dollars(breaks):
    return [f"${v:,.0f}" if v is not None else "" for v in breaks]


# Years shown, and the school year whose dollars amounts are expressed in.
FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR = 2016, cc.REAL_DOLLAR_YEAR
DOLLARS = f"{cc.school_year_label(cc.REAL_DOLLAR_YEAR)} dollars"

# Current operating spending per pupil, nominal (current_pp) and adjusted for
# inflation (current_pp_real).
spend = cc.to_real(
    cc.spending_for(cc.GRAPH_GROUP).filter(
        pl.col("year_end").is_between(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR)
    ),
    ["current_pp"],
)

# --- Checks: the numbers written out in the prose must match the data. --------
assert (FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR) == (2016, 2025) and DOLLARS == "2024–25 dollars"
_first = spend.filter(pl.col("year_end") == FIRST_YEAR)
_last = spend.filter(pl.col("year_end") == LAST_YEAR)
_chg = _first.join(_last, on="district", suffix="_last").with_columns(
    real_chg=pl.col("current_pp_real_last") - pl.col("current_pp_real"),
    nominal_chg=pl.col("current_pp_last") - pl.col("current_pp"),
).sort("real_chg", descending=True)
_cam = _chg.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)
assert round(_last.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)["current_pp"].item(), -3) == 31_000
assert round(_last["current_pp"].mean(), -3) == 30_000
assert round(_cam["real_chg"].item(), -2) == 3_300
assert round(_cam["real_chg"].item() / _cam["current_pp_real"].item() * 100) == 12
assert round(_cam["nominal_chg"].item(), -3) == 10_000
assert _chg["district"][0] == "Greenwich" and round(_chg["real_chg"][0], -3) == 6_000
assert _chg["district"].to_list().index(cc.FOCUS) == 2  # third of five: the middle
assert (_chg["real_chg"] > 0).all()  # every district rose after inflation
# Cambridge and Salem hold the top two places in every year shown.
for _y in range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1):
    _top2 = spend.filter(pl.col("year_end") == _y).sort("current_pp", descending=True)
    assert set(_top2["district"][:2]) == {"Cambridge", "Salem"}, _y
_idx = cc.load_price_index()
_infl = (
    _idx.filter(pl.col("year_end") == LAST_YEAR)["index_value"].item()
    / _idx.filter(pl.col("year_end") == FIRST_YEAR)["index_value"].item()
    - 1
)
assert round(_infl * 100) == 33
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-spending-per-pupil
#| fig-cap: "Current operating spending per K–12 pupil, adjusted for inflation (2024–25 dollars), by school year ending, 2016 (2015–16) through 2025 (2024–25). Source: NYS Comptroller local-government financial data; K-12 enrollment from NYSED; Consumer Price Index from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics."
g = spend.select("district", "year_end", "current_pp_real").drop_nulls()
cambridge = g.filter(pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS)

(
    ggplot(g, aes("year_end", "current_pp_real", color="district"))
    + geom_line(size=1)
    + geom_point(size=1.8)
    + geom_line(cambridge, size=2.4)  # emphasize the focus district
    + scale_color_manual(
        values=cc.PALETTE, name="", limits=cc.district_order(cc.GRAPH_GROUP)
    )
    + scale_x_continuous(breaks=list(range(FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR + 1)))
    + scale_y_continuous(labels=_dollars)
    + labs(
        x="School year ending",
        y=f"Spending per pupil ({DOLLARS})",
        title="Current operating spending per K-12 pupil, 2015–16 to 2024–25",
        subtitle=f"Adjusted for inflation; {DOLLARS}",
    )
    + cc.theme_ccs()
)
```

Every district's line rises over the decade, even after adjusting for
inflation, but the rank order barely changes.

Where each district started, where it ended, and the decade's change:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-spending-per-pupil-change
#| tbl-cap: "Current operating spending per K–12 pupil in 2015–16 and 2024–25, with change, by district (adjusted for inflation; 2024–25 dollars)."
t = spend.filter(pl.col("year_end").is_in([FIRST_YEAR, LAST_YEAR]))

wide = (
    t.with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("region") == "Washington County").then(0).otherwise(1).alias("_rank")
    )
    .pivot(values="current_pp_real", index=["_rank", "region", "district"], on="year_end")
    .sort(["_rank", "district"])
    .drop("_rank")
)

wide = wide.with_columns((pl.col("2025") - pl.col("2016")).alias("chg"))

(
    GT(wide, rowname_col="district", groupname_col="region")
    .tab_header(
        title="Current operating spending per pupil",
        subtitle="School-year-ending 2016 (2015–16) and 2025 (2024–25), in 2024–25 dollars"
    )
    .fmt_currency(columns=["2016", "2025", "chg"], decimals=0)
    .tab_spanner(label="School year ending", columns=["2016", "2025"])
    .cols_label(chg=md("Change<br>2016→2025"))
    .tab_style(
        style=[style.fill(color="#FCEFB4"), style.text(weight="bold")],
        locations=[
            loc.body(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
            loc.stub(rows=pl.col("district") == cc.FOCUS),
        ],
    )
    .tab_source_note(
        md(
            "**Source:** New York State Comptroller local-government financial "
            "data (expenditures); K-12 enrollment from NYSED. Current operating "
            "spending = General, Special Aid and School Lunch funds, excluding "
            "capital outlay, debt service and interfund transfers. Adjusted "
            "for inflation with the Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) and shown in "
            "2024–25 dollars; year = school-year-ending (2025 = 2024–25)."
        )
    )
)
```

**Cambridge's spending per pupil rose about $3,300 after inflation**, or about
12% — a middle-of-the-pack increase (Greenwich's was largest at about $6,000).
Before adjusting for inflation the increase was about $10,000; consumer prices
rose about 33% over the period. What sets Cambridge apart is
where it started — near the top in 2015–16 — and where it remains in 2024–25.
Whether that level is sustainable as enrollment falls is taken up in the
[Taxes](taxes.qmd) chapter.
